name: Select external managers and negotiate mandates
summary: External Portfolio Management picks hedge fund and public market managers to run part of the fund's money alongside its internal programs, and negotiates fee terms that pay managers mainly for performance. After a manager passes an informal screen, the team analyses the track record, meets the managers, sends a due diligence questionnaire and runs investment diligence and reference calls, while Risk checks overlap with internal programs, Investment Operations runs independent operational due diligence and Compliance and Legal review conflicts and fund documents. The principal then negotiates fees and terms, a memo goes through the director and managing director to Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee, and the engagement is approved by the CEO under delegation or by the Board's Investment Strategy Committee. Waiting for managers' answers, meeting slots and committee dates takes most of the four to six months, and cases drop out at screening, operational review, fee talks or committee.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager whose External Portfolio Management group keeps relationships with more than 60 asset managers across equities, credit, rates, currencies and commodities.
baseline.notes: A case starts when EPM opens a formal review of a manager for a mandate; the triage of unsolicited pitches before that is outside the count.

trigger: A program mandate calls for a new or replacement manager, or a manager's offering passes EPM's informal screen, and the team opens a formal review.
end_state: The engagement is approved by the PEC and by the CEO or the Investment Strategy Committee, the manager is notified and the terms are handed to Legal and operations, or the review is closed with a recorded decline.

volume.seasonality: No strong seasonality; more searches when a new external program is launched, as with the emerging markets directional program in F2021.

evidence.note: Process map estimate; EPM has more than 60 managers (F2021), so about 12 formal reviews a year implies modest roster turnover and new mandates.
A CMF managing director heads External Portfolio Management and sponsors the memo. FTE from about 3 hours per case.
An EPM director reviews and presents the memo. FTE is the author's estimate.
EPM portfolio managers run investment diligence and fee negotiation. FTE is the author's estimate from about 45 hours per case.
Senior associates analyse track records, call references and draft memos. FTE is the author's estimate.
Associates manage questionnaires, document requests and logging. FTE is the author's estimate.
Operational due diligence sits outside the investment team at most institutions; here in Investment Operations funds operations. FTE is the author's estimate.
Not listed in the process map's roles; the director of private investment operations is assumed to sign off the ODD rating. FTE from about 1.5 hours per case.
Risk checks exposure overlap and liquidity terms during diligence. FTE is the author's estimate.
Legal counsel reviews fund documents and key terms before approval. FTE is the author's estimate.
Compliance reviews conflicts and disclosures independently before approval. FTE is the author's estimate.

roles.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
roles.department: Office of the President and CEO

evidence.note: The Board delegates to the CEO appointments of external managers below a defined size. FTE from about 30 minutes per delegated case.

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Risk analytics platform (potential loss, limits, stress tests)
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Compliance system for personal trading, attestations and restricted lists

steps.name: Open the review and gather materials
steps.description: An EPM associate logs the manager in the deal pipeline system against the program mandate it would fill, arranges a non-disclosure agreement and collects the pitch book, monthly return history and offering documents.

error.defect_description: The return history received is a marketing composite rather than the fund's own record.

evidence.note: EPM evaluates managers to complement internal programs; most pitches are rejected before a formal review starts. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Analyse track record and strategy fit
steps.description: A senior associate analyses the return series for risk-adjusted performance, drawdowns, factor exposures and correlation with the fund's internal programs and existing managers, and estimates the strategy's capacity and the fees it would cost.

error.defect_description: Returns are analysed gross of fees or with backfilled history.

evidence.note: A manager must provide risk-adjusted value that more than offsets external fees. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Meet the manager and decide whether to proceed
steps.description: A principal meets the portfolio manager, tests the strategy story against the analysis and decides with the director whether to open full due diligence or decline.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Board-approved framework for engaging external managers: demonstrated expertise and value net of fees

evidence.note: Preliminary calls screen managers before intensive diligence. Decline share is the author's estimate for managers already past the informal pipeline screen.

steps.name: Send the due diligence questionnaire and document list
steps.description: The associate sends the AIMA-style due diligence questionnaire with the hedge fund module and a list of documents: offering memorandum, fund agreements, audited financials, regulatory filings, compliance manual, valuation policy and controls reports.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: DDQs are an early diligence step; standard document requests before the memo. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Manager completes the questionnaire
steps.description: The manager's investor relations, compliance and operations staff complete the questionnaire, often adapting a standard response, and upload the requested documents to a data room for the review team.

error.defect_description: Answers are incomplete or reuse an outdated standard response.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of manager response time for a full questionnaire.

steps.name: Review responses and log gaps
steps.description: The associate reads the responses against the questionnaire, checks each requested document arrived and is current, and lists missing or unclear answers for the manager.

error.defect_description: A stale controls report or missing document is not noticed.

evidence.note: Responses guide where to probe and follow-up questions. Share and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Manager supplies missing answers
steps.description: The manager answers the follow-up questions on the gap list and sends the missing or updated documents, usually after at least one reminder from the associate.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Run investment due diligence meetings
steps.description: The principal holds deep-dive sessions with the portfolio managers, risk manager and analysts, usually including an onsite visit or, in 2020 and 2021, a video visit, and tests how the edge, risk limits and team will hold up.

error.defect_description: A key-person dependence or style drift is not probed.

evidence.note: Onsite reviews are common for new managers, virtual during COVID-19. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Call references
steps.description: A senior associate calls three to five references, including other investors, former colleagues and service providers, and writes up what each said about the team, conduct and operations.

error.defect_description: A negative reference is recorded too mildly.

evidence.note: Reference checks with other investors and industry contacts. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Risk checks exposure overlap and liquidity terms
steps.description: A Risk senior associate maps the strategy's factor and position exposures against internal programs and existing managers, checks leverage and the fit of redemption terms with the fund's liquidity needs, and sends a note to the deal team.

error.defect_description: Overlap is understated because the manager's exposure report is at a coarse level.

evidence.note: Risk checks overlap with internal programs (process map). Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review operational documents
steps.description: A senior associate in funds operations reviews the valuation policy, administrator and custodian arrangements, auditor, controls reports, compliance manual, cyber security and business continuity, and lists the high-risk areas for the meeting.

error.defect_description: A weakness in independent valuation or cash controls is missed.

control.basis: Operational due diligence performed by Investment Operations, independent of the investment team

evidence.note: Most dedicated ODD teams report outside the investment function and collect documents before meetings. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Hold the operational due diligence meeting
steps.description: The ODD reviewer meets the manager's chief operating officer, chief financial officer and compliance officer, walks through the high-risk areas and trade-to-cash flows, and confirms key facts with the administrator.

error.defect_description: An administrator confirmation is skipped when the manager is late.

evidence.note: ODD meetings now run at least twice as long as a couple of hours; full ODD at the start of a relationship. Waits are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Sign off the operational due diligence rating
steps.description: The director of private investment operations reviews the ODD report and rating, agrees any conditions the manager must meet and signs off, or rejects the manager on operational grounds.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Independent ODD sign-off with a right to reject on operational grounds

evidence.note: About a third of dedicated ODD teams have a formal veto, used rarely. Shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Run compliance and conflict checks
steps.description: A compliance officer screens the manager, fund and principals against sanctions and adverse news, checks placement agent and political contribution disclosures and staff conflicts of interest, and signs a compliance note.

error.defect_description: A related-party link of a principal is missed.

control.basis: Code of Conduct conflict of interest procedures and anti-corruption policy

evidence.note: Independent compliance review before approval; the Board sets conflict and anti-corruption policies. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review fund documents and mandate terms
steps.description: Legal counsel reviews the offering memorandum, fund agreements or the managed account agreement and lists terms to negotiate: liquidity and gates, transparency, key person, most favoured nation rights, indemnities and fee mechanics.

error.defect_description: A gate or side pocket provision is not flagged.

control.basis: Legal review of fund documents before commitment

evidence.note: Counsel reviews and negotiates terms against preferred terms. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Negotiate fees and key terms
steps.description: The principal proposes the fee structure and terms: a lower management fee, a performance fee only above a hurdle, part of the fee deferred or treated as an advance on performance fees, a longer commitment for lower fees, capacity and co-investment rights, plus the legal points from counsel.

error.defect_description: An agreed fee term is recorded wrongly in the term sheet.

evidence.note: EPM trades lower management for higher performance fees, longer commitments for lower fees, fees as advances on performance fees, hurdles and co-investments; 1-or-30 style structures. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Manager responds to the term proposal
steps.description: The manager reviews the proposal with its counsel and replies with accepted terms, a counter-proposal or a refusal; strong or capacity-constrained managers concede little.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Fees are limited when managers cannot accept new capital; strong managers charge more. Shares and wait are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Draft the investment memo
steps.description: A senior associate writes the memo recommending the engagement: strategy and role in the program, track record, diligence and reference findings, risk overlap, ODD rating, compliance note, fee terms and expected value net of fees.

error.defect_description: Figures in the memo disagree with the final terms or analysis.

evidence.note: External manager appointments have written mandates and compensation arrangements; recommendation memos summarise diligence. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Director reviews the memo
steps.description: An EPM director challenges the recommendation, checks the figures and the fit with the program mandate and returns the memo for changes when needed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Managing director sponsors the memo
steps.description: The CMF managing director reads the memo, confirms the department sponsors the engagement within its mandate and authorises submission to Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities: department sponsorship before committee submission

evidence.note: Investment Management Authorities set approval authorities for departments and committees. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Present to the Portfolio Execution Committee
steps.description: The director submits the memo for Risk's independent opinion and to the Portfolio Execution Committee, waits for a meeting slot and presents the engagement; the committee approves, asks for more work or declines.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISRC sub-committee mandate: the PEC reviews new investments and manager engagements within Investment Management Authorities

evidence.note: The PEC reviews new investments with risk opinions and checks mandate alignment; larger items go to the Board. Split and wait are the author's estimates.

steps.name: CEO approves under delegated authority
steps.description: For engagements below the Board's size threshold, the President and CEO reviews the PEC-approved memo and signs the approval under authority delegated by the Board.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 34(b) (investment committee approves external manager engagements) with Board delegation to the CEO below a defined size

evidence.note: The Board approves external manager appointments as the Act requires, delegating those below a defined level to the CEO. Wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Investment Strategy Committee approves the engagement
steps.description: Larger engagements go through the board secretariat to the next meeting of the Board's Investment Strategy Committee, an outside body, which approves or declines the engagement.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 34(b) and ISC terms of reference 5.5(b): the investment committee approves engagement of external managers with discretionary authority

evidence.note: The ISC approves engagements above Board-set limits; eight regular ISC meetings in F2022. Wait to the next meeting is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Notify the manager and hand off for documentation
steps.description: The associate tells the manager the engagement is approved, sends the approved terms to Legal for final agreements and to funds operations for subscription and onboarding, and adds the manager to the monitoring list.

error.defect_description: A negotiated term is left out of the legal instruction.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; closing documents and subscription run in the legal closing and fund subscription processes.

exceptions.name: Declined after the first meeting
exceptions.description: The manager's story or analysis does not hold up and the review is closed before questionnaires are sent.

exceptions.name: Operational conditions or fail
exceptions.description: ODD finds weaknesses; the manager must fix them before approval (for example appoint an independent administrator), or the manager is rejected.

exceptions.name: Second round of fee negotiation
exceptions.description: The manager counters the fee proposal and the principal negotiates again; a few talks end without acceptable terms.

exceptions.name: Committee asks for more work
exceptions.description: The PEC asks for more analysis, for example on overlap with internal strategies, and the memo returns for redrafting.

exceptions.name: Board approval required
exceptions.description: The engagement exceeds the size delegated to the CEO and waits for the next Investment Strategy Committee meeting.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from opening the review to approval and handoff
benchmarks.population: Hedge fund and public market manager selections by institutional investors

evidence.note: A third of investors decide within three months and 38% spend at least six months evaluating a fund; the median is placed at about four and a half months for a review with committee and Board approval.

benchmarks.population: Preqin survey of over 100 hedge fund investors, 2015

evidence.note: 60% also conduct onsite reviews for new managers.

benchmarks.unit: CAD, fiscal 2022 (all external managers including private funds)

pain_points.description: Most of the elapsed time is waiting on managers for questionnaire answers, meetings and fee replies.

evidence.note: Author's reading of the step chain; long evaluation periods are common.

pain_points.description: Operational reviewers often lack time to finish before the investment team wants to commit, and findings can send the case back late.

evidence.note: A sizeable minority say they do not always have time to complete ODD reviews.

pain_points.description: Strong managers resist fee alignment terms, so negotiation takes rounds and sometimes ends the review.

evidence.note: Fee negotiation is limited when managers cannot accept new capital.

pain_points.description: Approval runs through director, managing director, Risk, PEC and then the CEO or Board committee, each on its own calendar.

evidence.note: Approval chain from Investment Management Authorities, PEC and Board delegation.

sources.title: The model fund F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)
sources.supports: TFM responsibilities (Strategic Exposures, current-year target exposures and range expectations, alignment of departments); Active Portfolio Management gives annual factor, geographic and sector guidance to 20 investment programs; Portfolio Design sets targeted allocation to programs within risk appetite and liquidity constraints; TFM's annual portfolio design process with departments and Risk over one- and five-year periods narrows each program to a preferred five-year deployment range; Balancing and Collateral group delivers required financial leverage; FCT executes financing and the term debt programme; External Portfolio Management has more than 60 managers and negotiates fees for alignment. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)
sources.supports: Strategic Portfolios: six asset classes and three regions, indicative allocations five years out (base plan public equity 23%, private equity 23%, public fixed income 32%, credit 17%, real assets 31%, cash and absolute return -27%); strategic mix of factor exposures and leverage reviewed at least triennially; CIO accountable for designing Strategic Portfolios and recommending market risk and leverage targets; ISRC with Portfolio Execution, Portfolio Strategy, Investment Risk and Operational and Legal Risk committees; Business Plan includes the Strategic Portfolios; leverage defined (term debt, commercial paper, secured borrowing, synthetic financing); recourse leverage C$122 billion in F2022, 18% to 25% of net assets over five years; Board limit of 45% of net assets from April 1, 2022, reviewed yearly with risk appetite; 10-day liquidity coverage ratio 2.9x against 1.0x; leverage-related expenses C$295 million. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: The model fund 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: Board governance of investment strategy: Risk Policy and risk appetite approved annually, Reference Portfolios, Business Plan with confirmation or adjustment of the Strategic Portfolios and Target Portfolios' allocation bands, Investment Statements; Board approves external manager appointments as required by the Act, delegating to the CEO those below a defined size; five key return-risk factors used in portfolio construction. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Terms of Reference for the Investment Strategy Committee (June 22, 2022)
sources.supports: The committee reviews the Investment Framework annually and the Reference and Strategic Portfolios at least every three years, receives quarterly reports on performance and pipelines, oversees criteria and process for selecting external managers with discretionary authority and approves their engagement as specified in the Authorities Policy. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Statement of Investment Objectives, Policies, Return Expectations and Risk Management for the Investment Portfolios of the Base plan and the Additional plan (version effective April 2, 2025)
sources.supports: Strategic Portfolios at Reference Portfolio risk (s. 5.3), reviewed at least triennially (s. 5.4), target allocations reviewed annually; Board approves market risk, liquidity and leverage limits annually (ss. 9.2, 9.5); leverage limits are a maximum relative to net assets; liquidity practices cover debt service, margin and transactions (s. 9.6); debt may be issued through a dedicated subsidiary with a guarantee (s. 8); transactions and external manager engagements above Board-set limits need ISC approval (s. 9.9). Later than the reference period; used for practice. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: SBAI 2024 Operational Due Diligence Practices Survey
sources.supports: 70% of institutional investors have dedicated ODD teams, 80% of them reporting outside the investment function; 77% do a full ODD review at the start of a new manager relationship; 60% conduct onsite reviews for new managers (7% do not, some used virtual reviews during COVID-19); results go to the investment committee alone for 50%; 32% of dedicated ODD teams have a formal veto, used rarely or at most once a year by 73% of them; a sizeable minority lack time to complete reviews. Later than the reference period; read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Operational due diligence: what are investors seeking? (AIMA Journal, edition 120)
sources.supports: ODD teams collect as many documents as possible before meetings and focus onsite time on high-risk areas; meetings now run at least twice as long as the couple of hours they once took; reviews cover compliance controls, valuation, service providers, independent administration, personnel and legal documents; requests on a week's notice are impractical.

sources.title: Due Diligence Questionnaires (2019 edition)
sources.supports: The 2019 AIMA Illustrative Questionnaire for the Due Diligence of Investment Managers with hedge fund, managed account, credit and other strategy modules and topic modules (cyber security, responsible investment, outsourcing); investors use it as an early step that guides follow-up questions and allows like-for-like comparison of managers.

sources.title: How investors source and select hedge funds (Preqin Investor Outlook H2 2015 excerpt)
sources.supports: Survey of over 100 hedge fund investors: about 13 proposals a month; 59% reject 95% or more at the first stage; 57% monitor 10 funds or fewer pre-investment; a third decide within three months of receiving a proposal and 38% spend at least six months evaluating a fund; sources are consultants (47%), own outreach (36%), peers (25%) and databases (21%).

sources.title: Hedge fund fees: should 1 or 30 be the new 2 and 20 (guest post from RCM Alternatives)
sources.supports: The 1-or-30 structure (1% management fee credited against a 30% share of alpha) reportedly designed by Albourne and the Teacher Retirement System of Texas; classic 2 and 20; average hedge fund management fee about 1.3% according to AIMA; strong or capacity-constrained managers charge more.

sources.title: External Investment Manager and Vehicle Selection Policy and Procedures (IMD-POL-1001)
sources.publisher: North Carolina Department of State Treasurer, Investment Management Division
sources.supports: Public pension manager selection: screen and short-form questionnaire, preliminary conference calls on operations, risk, compliance, conflicts and willingness to accept preferred terms, informal reference calls, finalist interviews with risk, operations and compliance; documents requested before the recommendation memo (compliance manual, SSAE 16 report and others); independent compliance review and signed compliance report before approval. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

assumptions: The unit counts formal reviews opened (about one a month); unsolicited pitches rejected in informal triage are not counted.

A Board decision starts a case when the Investment Strategy Committee approves a new external program or asks for a manager to be replaced; Board approval of individual engagements inside a case is the wait at s22.
Risk's formal opinion and the PEC meeting are separate processes; here they are folded into the wait at s20.
pio_director (ODD sign-off) and the CEO (delegated approval) are not in the process map's role list but are in the organisation file.
The split between CEO-delegated and Board approvals (60/40 of approved cases) is the author's estimate; the delegation threshold is not published.
Final legal agreements and subscription are handled in the legal closing and fund subscription processes after this workflow ends.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file.
